D006-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been serving as a pastor for over fifteen years, and for the past eight months, I’ve been seeing things—people in the pews during empty services, figures standing in my bedroom at night, sometimes even Jesus reaching out to me. I know they’re not really there, but they feel so real. I’ll catch myself talking to them, my words tripping over each other—like how the Bible says “out of the abundance of the heart, the mouth speaks”—but mine just rhymes sometimes: “light,” “fight,” “knight of the Lord.” I can’t stop it.

For about ten months now, I’ve been running nonstop—planning revivals, writing three sermons a day, repainting the church basement, jumping to new projects before finishing old ones. My wife says I don’t sleep, and my mood swings—sometimes I'm on top of the world, preaching with fire, then suddenly furious over a misplaced hymnal. But the past few months, that energy faded. I can’t feel joy in worship, can’t connect with my congregation, even my wife feels distant. Lately, I get this sudden urge to run into traffic—no plan, just… pull.

But the manic times? They were intense but brief—mostly those early months. The visions and voices have lasted far longer.
D006-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now, but things really started falling apart eight months ago. At first, I thought I was just stressed—running the salon, managing staff, being on my feet all day. But then I started feeling bugs crawling under my skin, like needles pricking me, even when I was clean. I’d scratch until I bled. I began believing the world was ending—like a machine had been activated underground and in six days, everything would just… stop. I told my clients, I even put up signs in the salon.

My speech? I don’t think I made sense anymore. Words just spilled out—mixing up thoughts, sentences crashing into each other. I’d start talking about highlights and end up yelling about satellites. For a while, I was bouncing off the walls—couldn’t sit down, couldn’t calm down. I’d start ten things: cleaning drawers, reorganizing product, calling old friends at 3 a.m., but couldn’t finish any of it. I felt high without being high.

But that intense energy? It only lasted a couple of months, off and on. Most of the time, I just couldn’t move. Didn’t open the salon for weeks. I tried to take pills all at once—just couldn’t handle the voices and the doom anymore. The wild mood swings weren’t constant—they came in bursts, but the delusions and hallucinations? They’ve been here the whole time.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h003.question: I’ve been struggling for almost a year now. At first, I started noticing things—like shadows moving in the corners of my classroom, kids who weren’t really there, or once, a man in a suit standing by the door during recess. I *know* he wasn’t real, but I *saw* him. That scared me. Then the thoughts got jumbled—sometimes I can’t piece my sentences together. I’ll start talking to my students or my husband and suddenly the words just… mix up. “The sky blue pencil runs” — that kind of thing. I’ve had these wild bursts of energy, like I can’t sit down, need to clean, plan lessons, dance—all at once. One night, I started ten crafts for my class and didn’t sleep. But those highs don’t last long—maybe a few days—then they’re gone. For three months last winter, I couldn’t get off the couch. I didn’t want to teach, didn’t want to live. I even saved pills, thinking… well, you know. And sometimes I feel like I’m meant to save the world with my mind—like I’m chosen. But that doesn’t make sense, right? The worst part is, the manic times are just scattered—short blips—while the voices, the visions, and the broken thoughts have been with me almost every day for eight months.
D006-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h004.question: I’ve been hearing voices for about eight months now—sometimes they’re whispering about me, other times they yell things, like I’m being watched or judged. I know people aren’t actually saying these things, but I *hear* them so clearly. Like the other day, the barista didn’t hand me my coffee directly, and I just *knew* he was sending me a secret message—everyone’s gestures feel loaded. School has become impossible. I’ll start chopping veggies for a dish and suddenly want to paint the kitchen walls or write a song, but I never finish anything. I used to love cooking, but now I jump from one thing to another, like my brain won’t let me focus. For a while, I felt on top of the world—like I didn’t need sleep, like I could run forever—but that only lasted a few weeks at a time, and then I’d crash. The last few months, I’ve barely left my room. I keep thinking about how I could just… disappear. I even figured out a way and where I’d do it. But here’s the thing—the high-energy phases, the racing ideas—they weren’t *most* of the time. The voices and the paranoia? Those have been constant. The manic-like stuff came and went, but the hallucinations? They’ve stayed.
D006-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h005.question:

For almost a year, I’ve been wired, like I can’t sit still. I’ll start practicing at 3 a.m., jump to composing, then pacing. I feel high one second, then furious the next—no reason. But it’s not real joy. The world’s ending, I know it. Everything’s collapsing. Music’s meaningless now. I don’t even go to rehearsals. I just... sit and wait. 

I don’t care about anything anymore. Not playing, not seeing friends. I think, “I wish I wasn’t here.” But that rage and energy? It came and went fast, especially compared to the voices, the smells, the thoughts that won’t stop. That’s been constant—nearly eight months of this. The rest? It flickered—intense, but short.
D006-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D005_h011.question:
